title: K-injective representative of the module derived exchange mate
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$ form a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], so $fg'=gf'$. Work in the constant-ring module categories $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and their unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use the exact inverse-image adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], with sheaf counits $\varepsilon_u^0$, and the derived functors, derived adjunctions and square comparison specified in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Write $Q_T$ for localization of complexes on $T$ into $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Let $\theta^0_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ be the module sheaf composition isomorphism whose termwise descent is the square comparison of that definition. Define $\Ex^0_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*g'^{-1}F$ to be the transpose of $g'^{-1}\varepsilon^0_{f,F}\circ\theta^0_{\square,f_*F}$ under the module adjunction, equivalently its unit-square-counit mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

For any $K\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, choose a K-injective complex $I$, an isomorphism $s:K\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XI$, and a quasi-isomorphism $j:g'^{-1}I\to J$ with $J$ K-injective [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. There is no boundedness assumption on $K,I,J$. Naturality of $\Ex^0$ gives a morphism of complexes, and put
$$e=f'_*(j)\circ\Ex^0_{\square,I}:g^{-1}f_*I\longrightarrow f'_*J.$$
Use the canonical K-injective direct-image comparisons of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], that is, the derived-functor comparisons $Q(u_*P)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*(QP)$ for K-injective $P$ of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], to define $\chi_{I,s}:Q_Y(f_*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K$ and $\chi_{J,t}:Q_{Y'}(f'_*J)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$, where $\varphi^u_P:u^{-1}Q_TP\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(u^{-1}P)$ is the exact termwise comparison for $u:S\to T$ in that definition and $t=Q_{X'}(j)\circ\varphi^{g'}_I\circ g'^{-1}(s)$. Thus $\chi_{I,s}$ is the canonical comparison $Q_Y(f_*I)\cong Rf_*Q_XI$ followed by $Rf_*(s^{-1})$, and $\chi_{J,t}$ is the canonical comparison $Q_{Y'}(f'_*J)\cong Rf'_*Q_{X'}J$ followed by $Rf'_*(t^{-1})$. Set
$$\sigma_{\rm src}=g^{-1}(\chi_{I,s})\circ(\varphi^g_{f_*I})^{-1},\qquad\sigma_{\rm tgt}=\chi_{J,t}.$$
The specified unbounded module exchange mate $\Ex_{\square,K}$ of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] satisfies
$$\Ex_{\square,K}\circ\sigma_{\rm src}=\sigma_{\rm tgt}\circ Q_{Y'}(e).$$
Consequently every such pair of representatives gives the same exchange morphism after these canonical identifications. In particular this applies to bounded below $K$, a bounded below injective resolution $I$ and any K-injective replacement $j$; no preservation of K-injectivity by $g'^{-1}$ is required.

proof.text: Normalize the exact derived inverse-image square using mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_hom_app_factorsh and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fach. Cancellation of the composition comparison gives exactly the homotopy-model normalization required by lem-pur-exact-derived-mate.

Apply derivedExact_mateEquiv_app_fac to the two inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions and their square. On quotient complexes identify mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh with mapDerivedCategoryFactors, the localized termwise mate with Q of the complex mate, and the homotopy-derived unit with rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ. This gives D(g inverse image)(gamma_I) followed by Ex_QI equal to the exact factor, Q(Ex0_I), gamma_(g prime inverse image I), and the derived direct image of the inverse exact factor.

Use naturality of Ex along s inverse, and naturality of rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ along j. Expand t: Q(j) followed by t inverse equals the inverse exact factor followed by D(g prime inverse image)(s inverse). Functoriality and cancellation of the exact comparison factors prove the desired representative equality. For K-injective I and J, rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_eq identifies the units with the inverses used in moduleExchangeDirectImageIso. The three original canonical-map definitions are unchanged.
